input.quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — far longer than twelve months — yet the only exits are the Indenture Trustee's for-cause removal on a continuing Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)) and natural run-off. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience exit for us. No Customer convenience termination right exists, failing both preferred and fallback (fallback element 1 is absent; there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target preferred: Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met, and the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end exit on 90 days' notice that the contract currently forecloses. New Section 7.7 designates the Issuer as the "Customer" and gives it an unconditional 30-day convenience termination with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees; the Section 8.3 edits add that exit to the termination list and reletter it cleanly as (a)/(b)/(c). We deliberately did not condition our exit on appointment of a Successor Servicer — that would qualify the unconditional right the checklist requires — and Sections 7.3/7.4 already engage on any termination "under this Agreement".

ops.text: Section 7.7 Termination for Convenience. The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services) may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, in which case the Servicer will refund to the Customer pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination.

ops.newText: This Agreement will terminate on the earliest to occur of (a) a termination under Section 7.7, (b) the date

ops.oldText: and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1
ops.newText: and (c) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added Section 7.7 so that we, as the Customer for the Servicer's services, may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of any prepaid fees, since the Agreement otherwise runs until the last Receivable is paid with only a for-cause removal right. We conformed Section 8.3's termination list to include that exit; Section 7.1's no-resignation bar on the Servicer is untouched.
proposal.summary: Add numbered Section 7.7 giving the Issuer (as Customer) a 30-day convenience termination with pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and conform/reletter Section 8.3.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
